candidate.title: SSA Employee Name & Fake Badge Impersonation Scam
candidate.summary: Scammers are pairing the real names of actual Social Security Administration and SSA-OIG employees with fabricated badge photos and fake social media profiles to convince victims they're talking to a genuine federal official before demanding payment.
relatedScams: Senior U.S. Official Impersonation Messaging Scam
FCC Commissioner Impersonation "Phone Number Under Investigation" Scam
safetyTips: Ignore unexpected outreach claiming to be from SSA or SSA-OIG, even if it includes a name and badge photo
Remember no legitimate government employee will ever send photos of badges or credentials, or demand immediate payment
Do not trust caller ID, since scammers can spoof government phone numbers
Create your own my Social Security account to help protect against identity thieves
Verify independently using publicly listed agency contact information rather than numbers or links given to you
Report fake social media profiles impersonating government employees directly to the platform
candidate.howItWorks: According to the SSA Office of the Inspector General, federal law enforcement agencies are seeing a surge in imposter scams that misuse real SSA and SSA-OIG employee names along with fabricated badge images and fraudulent social media profiles. Criminals pull information from an actual employee's social media profile to impersonate that real OIG staffer, using it to initiate contact and build trust with a potential victim. Once trust is established, the fake "employee" sends a doctored photo of a badge or credential to look legitimate, claims there is a problem with the victim's Social Security number, benefits, or identity, and pressures the person to act immediately, demanding payment through gift cards, precious metals, cryptocurrency, wire transfers, or cash.
redFlags: Someone claiming to be from SSA or SSA-OIG sends a photo of a badge or credential
Contact is initiated by referencing details that look like they came from a real employee's social media profile
Caller or messager demands immediate payment or personal/financial information
Payment is requested via gift cards, gold bars, cryptocurrency, wire transfer, or cash
Threats of arrest or legal action if you don't comply right away
realExamples: SSA-OIG's April 2026 scam alert describes criminals using the name of a real SSA employee along with a fake badge or credential to appear legitimate
The same alert describes scammers using information from social media profiles to impersonate a real SSA-OIG employee to initiate contact and build trust with potential victims
candidate.source: SSA Office of the Inspector General, https://oig.ssa.gov/scam-alerts/2026-04-28-new-wave-of-imposter-scams-criminals-using-real-ssa-employee-names-and-fake-badges/

triage.reasoning: This is the same core SSA impersonation scheme (claiming a problem with your SSN/benefits, pressuring immediate payment via gift cards/crypto/wire) already covered by "Social Security Number Suspended Scam," just with an added twist of using real employee names and fabricated badge photos/social media profiles for credibility; it's a refinement rather than a fundamentally new scam pattern.
